Planted bugs B05, B13, B14 and B16 (#73)

* Maintenance.Status, /health and /version, etcd's request size limit

- core: a write's size is the marshaled InternalRaftRequest with a
  10-byte request ID, as in etcd v3.7.2, so the largest accepted value
  matches etcd to the byte (#62). Reads have only gRPC's limit.
- core: Status answers Maintenance.Status with version 3.7.2, the
  leader, term, commit and applied indexes, quota and a nonzero size.
- server: with TLS the client port serves gRPC, GET /version and
  GET /health over HTTP/2 like etcd; RangeStream stays Unimplemented,
  which Kubernetes 1.37 falls back on.
- smoke: etcdctl endpoint status, /version and /health.
- difftest: the max-request-size steps now match etcd.

* Compact: MVCC compaction through Raft, watch cancels, simulated compactions

- mvcc: Store.Compact follows etcd: compacted and future revisions are
  refused, the revision stays, reads at the compaction work and below
  fail, a tombstone at the compaction stays for watches.
- core: Compact is an entry kind; a watch from below the compaction,
  or with prev_kv from it, gets etcd's compaction cancel with header
  revision 0.
- server: KV.Compact.
- difftest: the compaction cases now match etcd, with the stricter
  cancel at the compaction revision.
- sim: clients compact about once in 100 calls; the checks use the
  committed log replayed without compactions; a watch canceled by a
  compaction starts a new logical watch; liveness accepts definite
  answers.

* Address review of the API PR

- server: lift net/http's HTTP/2 limit of 250 streams per connection,
  as etcd does; TestManyStreamsOnOneConnection opens 300 watches.
- server: /health uses etcd's 7 s request timeout and reports the
  gRPC status message without its wrapper.
- core: Status takes header and body term from one snapshot and sets
  DowngradeInfo; the WAL record size comes from wal.EntryRecordBytes.
- The size limit matches etcd's strictest member ID case, which the
  code comment and design doc now say.

* Leases: grant, revoke, keepalive, expiry, TimeToLive and Leases

- core: State holds the index and the leases; Apply runs one committed
  write against both. Grants pick IDs before proposal and clamp TTLs
  like etcd; keys move between leases on every write; a revoke deletes
  a lease's keys at one revision, an empty lease moves none. The
  leader keeps expiry in ticks and proposes the revoke of an expired
  lease; a new leader gives every lease its full TTL. Keepalive is a
  Raft entry. TimeToLive and Leases are linearizable reads.
- core: watchers match only the changes of the write just applied; a
  grant or keepalive used to re-send the previous write's events.
- server: the Lease service with the KeepAlive stream.
- difftest: the lease cases match etcd; nothing is expected to fail.
- sim: clients grant, use, keep alive and revoke leases; the model
  replays through core.State; leases must expire by the end; the
  history gets an ambiguous expiry op per lease. Porcupine's short
  runs leave leases out, which made its search time out.

* Address review of Compact

- sim: half of the compactions land exactly where a disconnected watch
  will resume, the boundary where etcd's watch rules change; a cancel
  closes the abandoned stream in the core; only compacted and future
  revision count as definite answers.
- design.md: Compact's cost, and which checker validates compaction
  errors and cancels.
- Wording: the request size note says one or more bytes; a comment
  reflowed.

* sim: quiet period covers the last lease expiries

Seed 3 failed after the merge: a lease expired just before the run
ended and its delete reached the watch client after the end. The quiet
period after the clients stop is now the lease grace of 8 s plus 2 s.

* core: hold writes while the leader's append is on its way to disk

The leader proposed what arrived since the last turn, usually one write,
so it fsynced about once per write (1.8 writes per fsync at 256 clients
in the profiling pre-work on #50). Now, while it has an append with
entries in flight, Process holds new writes, and they go out as one
entry once that append is durable. The byte cap still sends a full
entry early. Hard-state-only appends hold nothing, followers forward at
once, and heartbeats, votes, ReadIndex, replies and watch events never
wait. TestWritesWaitForTheLeadersAppend holds one append, submits 50
writes and gets one entry of 50.

* core: gofumpt

* Address review of leases

- core: an expiry carries the leader's count of applied keepalives and
  applies only if it is still current, so a keepalive that commits
  first keeps the lease instead of being answered and then revoked.
  TestKeepAliveBeforeExpiryKeepsTheLease reproduces the review's case.
- core: Effects.Expired lists leases that expired as the node applied.
- sim: no lease may expire before its TTL ran out since its last
  successful grant or renewal; expiries in the log become the revokes
  they amount to; the model takes its minimum TTL from the config.
- design.md: the conditional expiry, and where leases differ from
  etcd (keepalive through Raft, follower TimeToLive).

* sim: watches stay open once the clients stop

CI seed 676605047 (TestLinearizable) failed with "watch 3 was never
created": a drop scheduled before the clients stopped fired after, and
its reopen, up to 2 s later, fell after the end of the run. Drops now do
nothing once the clients stop.

* Disk faults in the simulator, a stalled leader fences itself, erase-one-disk

- sim: failed writes and syncs (EIO, short write with ENOSPC) stop the
  node, which never retries and restarts from its disk; disk stalls of
  1.5 to 4 s; damaged synced bytes at a crash must make the node refuse
  to start, and it stays fenced; at a checkpoint during the faults and
  at the end, every node's disk is erased in turn and the other two
  cold-start alone and must hold every acknowledged write.
- core: a leader whose own append has been on its way to disk for two
  election timeouts stops (ErrDiskStalled), so its clients go
  elsewhere; TestStalledLeaderIsReplaced checks it with a scripted
  stall.
- simfs: Durable copies, Corrupt, short writes, ClearFaults.

* Address recheck and Astra review of leases

- core: expiries carry the lease's stamp, taken from one counter that
  every grant and keepalive advances, so a stale expiry never hits a
  lease granted again with the same ID (TestStaleExpiryLeavesANewGrant).
- core: the leader arms a lease for its TTL plus one tick, so a grant
  late in a tick never expires early (TestLeaseNeverExpiresEarly); the
  simulator's lower bound loses its one-tick slack.
- core: TimeToLive rounds the leader's remaining seconds down, as etcd.
- Comments rewrapped.

* Address review of batching

- core: writes wait only for the append that carries the leader's own
  last batch; appends of forwarded proposals no longer hold them, so
  steady follower traffic cannot starve local writes
  (TestForwardedWritesDoNotHoldLocalOnes fails with the old rule).
  A leadership change resets the wait.
- core: each write counts its framing toward the byte cap, so empty
  requests cannot pile up behind a held append (TestByteCapSendsAn-
  EntryEarly); a write that timed out while waiting is dropped.
- TestHardStateAppendHoldsNothing: a write behind a commit-index-only
  append goes out at once.
- design.md: what the hold waits for, and that the byte cap bounds an
  entry, not a disk group.

* core: gocritic in batch test

* tigerstore: run with at least two Go processors

The batch256 pre-work on #47 found that a blocking fsync keeps the only
Go processor when GOMAXPROCS is 1, so request intake, peer sends and
replies wait for the disk and the leader writes about one request per
fsync. Two processors on the same CPU took 256 clients from 1.2 to 53
writes per leader fsync. The committer stays one goroutine.

* Network, pause and clock faults in the simulator

- Each link change draws new delays per directed link, so delays
  switch and directions differ; directed links stall for 0.5 to 2 s
  and then deliver in order; processes pause for 0.2 to 2 s.
- Clocks drift up to 5% per node and jump forward by up to 3 ticks, at
  most once per node in 10 s; the lease lower bound allows for that
  declared envelope.
- TestAllLinkMasks holds each of the 64 directed-link sets, then heals,
  with every checker; TestSwitchingLinks switches masks every ~300 ms.
- Liveness exempts calls to a paused node.

* sim: lint

* WIP: planted bugs

* Address review of disk faults

- Corrupt is a misdirected write into a sealed segment, never the
  newest one; the simulator uses 32 KiB segments.
- An injected I/O error during recovery is a failed boot, retried later.
- Erase-one-disk checks every entry applied by the checkpoint against
  the final log, so deletes, leases and revisions count too.
- TestSeeds requires a disk fault in every run, and a fenced node and a
  stopped stalled leader over 64 or more seeds. The once-per-run fault
  retries until a node is up to take it.
- Healing finishes a write held back by a stall.
- TestStalledLeaderIsReplaced bounds when the leader stops.
- Separate event kinds for the once fault and the leader stall; no
  impossible guard in the watchdog count; docs.

* Address review of network faults

- Pauses only grow, hold events in a FIFO until the node resumes, and
  end at a crash; healing lets them and link stalls run out, so nothing
  overtakes what they hold. A paused node closes watch streams through
  its own event, and the simulator fails a run if a paused node works.
- A link stall also holds what is already on the link.
- The simulator numbers messages per link and fails on any reordering.
- Half-open links: the sender keeps its connection while messages
  vanish, until the write timeout fails it and Raft hears the peer is
  unreachable. TestHalfOpenLink bounds the healthy pair.
- Each net fault also comes once per run, retried until it takes
  effect; TestSeeds requires each, and an asymmetric link over 64+
  seeds. TestAllLinkMasks checks the mask went in;
  TestEachNetFaultTakesEffect runs each fault alone.
- No pause exemption in the liveness rule; delays drawn once; docs.

* sim: what a node sends on a stream the client already left goes nowhere

A paused node handles a stream close only when it resumes, so it can
still answer the stream before that. After it handles the close, an
answer is still a failure.

* Planted bugs: B11 on Linux fsync semantics, B15, inventory in CI and docs

* Gray nodes and clients, crashes inside recovery, and a commit watchdog

- core: a leader whose own entries wait three election timeouts to
  commit stops (ErrCommitStalled), so a gray leader whose heartbeats get
  through but whose appends do not cannot hold the cluster.
- sim: gray periods with a changing gray node (appends dropped, slow
  fsync half the time), a gray watch client that never reads and
  reconnects every 50 to 300 ms, and crashes at the first to fourth
  writing operation inside wal.Open.
- TestGrayLeaderIsReplaced bounds the stop and the healthy pair;
  TestEachFaultTakesEffect covers the new faults; TestSeeds floors.

* sim: a disk fault in every run that appends; difftest: a watch may end at its deadline from either side

The guaranteed disk fault waited for a sync that a stall could hold
until healing, or for a node that never wrote again. It is now due in
the first 5 s and fails the write of the next append with entries.
Runs in which no node appended from then until healing are counted,
and may be at most one seed in 16. Link changes are at most 6 s apart.

The difftest watch step ends at a 1 s deadline; the server can end the
stream first with Canceled.

* planted: B11 only on a failed sync; a Raft panic in a planted run counts as caught

* core: hold peer messages until a new term or vote is durable; sim: the guaranteed disk fault always fires; difftest: watch steps end on a progress notification

Raft with async storage writes sends a candidate's vote requests before
its own term and vote are durable. In TestLinearizable seed 690901131 a
node won term 1, lost its term in a failed write, restarted in term 0
and won term 1 again with an empty log; two nodes applied different
entries at index 2. The core now holds every message to a peer while an
append that changes the term or vote is on its way to disk.

The guaranteed disk fault stays due after healing if no node appended
during the faults, and fires on the first append then; the liveness
rule starts that much later. TestSeeds fails a run without a disk fault.

The difftest watch step asks for progress after each response and ends
on the progress notification, so the stream never ends on a timer.

* sim: a disk fault after healing moves the liveness rule and the clients' stop with it

* Address reviews of planted bugs

- A catch counts only when the failure is the bug's expected assertion;
  anything else, and any crash, fails. One subtest per seed. No panic
  recovery.
- The simulator fails a node that recovers less than it last reported
  durable; B02, B03, B04b, B11 and B12 are caught by it.
- B06d sends progress ahead of queued events at a real revision; B04b
  cuts the last synced record and recovers again; lastStart comes from
  replay. B15's budget is 32.
- docs/testing.md holds the inventory with assertions, budgets, status,
  deferrals and deviations. CI lints the planted tag; planted jobs get
  30 minutes. checkers uses independent.

* planted: B04c, a decodable flipped payload bit that recovery accepts without its checksum; approved deviations in docs

* wal: lint

* Address reviews of gray faults

- Recovery crashes fail every write from the cut on, only for a node
  with a log, at any of the first six writes (the first two until one
  crash happened); a due recovery crash also crashes the next node that
  writes entries before its sync, so a torn tail needs repair.
- GrayNodes counts gray nodes that lost an append, GrayStreams streams
  whose watches exist; the guaranteed gray period lasts until a drop
  and moves on from a down node. Half the gray periods stay on the
  leader; TestSeeds requires gray-leader commit stops over 64 seeds.
- Link stalls and pauses end by healing.
- A watch client handles a broken stream only if it is still the one
  that broke (seed 48).
- TestGrayClient bounds other calls beside the gray client; docs say
  slow reading is left to the real-process tests.
- Corruption at one crash in two and 8 KiB segments, so damaged disks
  are common enough for the 64-seed floor.

* sim: stalls and pauses end by healing; a watch client handles only its current stream breaking

Seeds 467 and 709164578 had a link stall or pause that ran past healing
and cost a leader 2.5 s after it. A broken-stream event for a stream the
client already left reopened its watch a second time.

* Planted bugs B05, B13, B14 and B16

- B05 and B16 replace the snapshot and segment-cleaning bugs, as the
  owner decided on #47: a new WAL segment used before its directory
  entry is synced, and rotation without the old segment's last sync.
  The simulator catches both as lost durable appends.
- B13 blocks the node driver on a slow watch stream; TestSlowWatcherIsCut
  in internal/node requires the stream closed and writes and reads
  within 10 election timeouts (node.Config.WatchQueue for the test).
- B14 removes the peer write deadline; TestStalledPeerIsDropped in
  internal/peer stalls one connection through a proxy and requires a
  later message over a new one.
- Each of those packages has its own TestPlanted; CI runs all three.

* sim: a stream break names its node too

* planted: a liveness failure never counts as a catch; B04c only on diverged or wrong state

* sim: recovery may end below what was reported durable where an unsynced write replaced it; liveness 2 s later with a node fenced; B10 may be caught by the watch checker

* Address reviews of B05, B13, B14 and B16

- The node and peer TestPlanted count only their scenario's detecting
  failure (errSlowWatcher, errNotDropped); setup failures fail.
- The B14 proxy stalls the connections open at stallOpen, and the test
  waits until the held one stopped reading; it then requires a second
  connection and an unreachable report.
- docs: B16's replacement explained as the nearest step, not the same
  class; the two new tests in the baseline sentence; import grouping.

* server: with one peer link stalled, writes commit within 10 election timeouts through the healthy quorum (B14's quorum check)

* server: the quorum check stalls the leader's link and runs until its writer hits the write deadline

* sim: hold a stalled link's messages in order; nodes stopped after healing move the liveness rule; liveness from 4 s after healing; B04c flips only entry payloads

- A link stall moves every message on the link to the stall's end in
  the order sent, one nanosecond apart; seed 721530657 had one due
  exactly at the end overtake those held back.
- Any node stopped after healing (late disk fault, a watchdog whose wait
  began before) moves the liveness rule and the clients' stop.
- Liveness starts 4 s after healing: one election for a node restarted
  then, and one more when a node with a higher term and a shorter log
  makes the new leader step down (seed 721530481). Short runs heal 8 s.
- wal.PayloadEnds read the record body one byte late and took hard
  states for entries; B04c now flips entry payloads only.
- The merge left B04c's block in maybeCorrupt twice.

* sim: only a stop in the first LiveAfter of healing moves the liveness rule

* server: the quorum check waits for a leader and counts reconnects from the stall

* server: format

Raft with async storage writes sends a candidate's vote requests before
its own term and vote are durable. In TestLinearizable seed 690901131 a
node won term 1, lost its term in a failed write, restarted in term 0
and won term 1 again with an empty log; two nodes applied different
entries at index 2. The core now holds every message to a peer while an
append that changes the term or vote is on its way to disk.

The guaranteed disk fault stays due after healing if no node appended
during the faults, and fires on the first append then; the liveness
rule starts that much later. TestSeeds fails a run without a disk fault.

The difftest watch step asks for progress after each response and ends
on the progress notification, so the stream never ends on a timer.
